subject: Private deployment maintenance: proposed window, version pin policy, and rollback plan
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-retail.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@corpcloud.io
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Upcoming maintenance window for private deployment - request

Hi Rachel,

We're planning to apply OS and runtime security patches for our private Redwood deployment in our us-west VPC cluster. We'd like to schedule a maintenance window sometime the week of Sep 6. Before we lock anything in, can you confirm Redwood's expectations for: version pinning, KV-cache invalidation, and a rollback path if model-serving latency regresses?

Key constraints on our side:
- Business hours: we prefer 02:00-04:00 UTC (low traffic)
- Need at least 30 minutes of post-patch verification before traffic is routed back
- Audit requirement: screenshot/evidence of model version and package checksums

Can your team share a proposed maintenance matrix (steps, estimated duration, and owners)? Also, we may involve CorpCloud for node-level updates (CC'd).

Thanks,
Lena
Site Reliability Manager
Acme Retail

Attachment: maintenance_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-retail.com>, ops@corpcloud.io
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-22T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming maintenance window for private deployment - proposed plan

Hi Lena — thanks for the heads up. See below a concise proposal and next steps; attaching a more detailed rollback checklist.

High level proposal (can adjust):
- Proposed window: 2026-09-08 02:00-04:30 UTC (2.5 hrs)
- Patch sequence: (1) infra OS kernel & Docker security updates on standby nodes, (2) drain & patch model-serving node pool, (3) pin model artifact versions at start of rollout, (4) apply runtime patch and quick smoke (60s), (5) 30m canary ramp on 5% traffic, (6) full traffic roll.
- Verification: smoke tests (latency P50/P95), functional prompts from the Acme prompt set, KV cache consistency check.
- Rollback trigger: >10% request error increase or >25% P95 latency regression sustained for 10m during canary.

Attachments: rollback_checklist.md (detailed steps), proposed_changes.patch (diff for runtime config).

Next steps:
1) Dev/infra alignment on drain order and snapshot timing.
2) Security to confirm audit artifacts and checksums.
3) CorpCloud to confirm node reboot timing.

I'll loop in Dev and Soojin to align the operator runbook.

Cheers,
Rachel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming maintenance window - internal ops plan and version pin specifics

Rachel / team — sketching out the technical plan and pinning details:

Version pinning:
- We'll snapshot the running model artifact (SHA256) and record the config hash before any change. The rollout will reference the snapshot; any new model binary will be treated as a separate deploy.
- For runtime libs, we'll pin to the exact wheel/tarball + checksum in the deployment manifest (we'll include the full SBOM in the audit artifact).

Caching / KV notes:
- We'll keep prefix cache warm for top-20 prefixes; full KV invalidation is NOT necessary unless we update tokenizer or model weights.
- After the node pool patch, we'll run a KV integrity check across shards (takes ~4–6 minutes).

Rollback approach:
- Maintain pre-patch image tags and keep the previous runtime pool in cold standby for 30 minutes post-patchization (no traffic).
- Rollback steps (high level): scale up pre-patch pool -> shift canary traffic -> run smoke tests -> scale down patched pool. Expect rollback duration ~12–20 minutes.

Operational cautions:
- If a model version regression is detected, do NOT perform a rolling restart during rollback; use traffic routing only.
- We must avoid concurrent DB schema changes during this window.

I'll prepare simple automation scripts to do the snapshot/pin and the canary traffic shift (JIRA PRIV-4321). Markus — can you confirm the estimated node drain times for the current cluster image?

Thanks,
Dev
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming maintenance window - drain timings and verification

Quick confirmation on drain timings and one operational ask:

- Current on-prem node drain (median): 6m per node; cold reboot 3–4m. For a 10-node serving pool we should budget ~70m for sequential drain/patch/rejoin if done serially.
- Recommendation: parallelize into two batches (5 nodes each) to keep total time under 40–45m for the node patch phase. This matches the 2.5 hr window with buffer.

Security ask from my side: include an independent check that the model checksum recorded post-patch matches the snapshot (hannah — can your team run the verification script and sign off?). Also want to avoid KV shard resync during the canary — instead run integrity check after batch completion.

Markus
Engineering Manager, Dedicated Deployments
Redwood Inference
